PullRequest.Title: Fix flaky notebook outline tests and helper cleanup
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-engineering#3873.

- Use UUIDs instead of millisecond timestamps for mock notebook editor IDs. Editors created in the same millisecond could otherwise share a cached outline data source, causing a non-empty cell to be reported as "empty cell".
- Put cleanup in `try/finally` in both notebook test helpers. A failing assertion previously skipped disposal and caused the subsequent `LanguagesRegistry` leak failure. Successful callbacks retain their results and cleanup order; failing callbacks now clean up before propagating their error.

Scenarios.Scenario: Notebook tests create a mock editor, optionally acquire outline data, run the callback, and complete successfully
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The helper constructs one in-process notebook model/editor, invokes and awaits the test callback, then disposes the editor/model/store before resolving. Successful callbacks already reached the same cleanup synchronously after the await before this diff; only the editor ID calculation changes on this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One ID generation per mock notebook editor; withTestNotebook creates one editor and withTestNotebookDiffModel creates two. Outline cache cardinality is one entry per concurrently referenced editor after ReferenceCollection keying, rather than accidental sharing when virtual Date.now values collide.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each helper awaits one callback and performs cleanup serially. The diff helper creates two editors serially. There is no added Promise.all, queue, limiter bypass, or aggregate concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: NotebookCellOutlineDataSourceFactory keys its ReferenceCollection by editor.getId(). UUIDs make each editor's cold cache entry distinct; references are destroyed on disposal. There is no warm cross-editor cache that is valid to preserve, and no negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed helper, UUID implementation, cache key consumer, representative callers, and disposal path were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact suite-wide mock-editor count was not enumerated, but each added UUID operation is bounded O(1) and test-only; model construction, callback work, and successful cleanup dominate and are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. Replacing Date.now().toString() with generateUuid() adds only one bounded in-process crypto UUID operation per editor and prevents invalid cache aliasing; it does not introduce realistic latency, throughput, memory, or concurrency degradation.

Scenarios.Scenario: withTestNotebook callback rejects or throws while virtual timers are installed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After callback failure there is no successful product/test progress remaining; the helper must restore virtual-time globals and propagate the error. The new finally disposes one editor, view model, text model, and disposable store before rejection escapes, while runWithFakedTimers then restores globals without draining the timer queue.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cleanup is bounded to the resources owned by one helper invocation and scales with that test notebook's cells/listeners. It runs once per failed invocation, not per timer, frame, or event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The callback is awaited; cleanup is serial and executes once. Virtual scheduling is cancelled after the helper callback settles, with no new concurrent boundary work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No persistent cache lookup is introduced. Disposal releases helper-owned models, lists, services, listeners, and any reference-counted outline state instead of leaving them live after failure.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the previous await bypassed all following cleanup when it rejected; the added finally directly guarantees cleanup, and the virtual-timer wrapper's failure semantics were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Disposal duration varies with notebook cell count, but it occurs only on an already-failing test path and bounds retained memory rather than amplifying it.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The change improves cleanup lifecycle and retained-memory behavior on failures; successful-path work and ordering remain unchanged.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The helper creates two in-process notebook editors/models, awaits the diff-test callback, disposes both model graphs and the shared store in finally, then propagates failure. On successful callbacks, disposal already occurred before return in the base code.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly two editor/model graphs per invocation, each scaling with its supplied original or modified cell array; cleanup executes once per failed invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Original and modified test editors are created and disposed serially, and the callback is awaited. No concurrent subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network fan-out is reachable from the changed helper path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Any helper-owned caches and disposable references are released with the shared store. No new cache, cache miss fan-out, or unbounded key retention is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both the helper implementation and representative diff-test callers were inspected; all changed work is local lifecycle cleanup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cleanup cost depends on supplied cell counts, but this is bounded teardown on a failure path and prevents the larger cost of retaining both graphs.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. The finally block removes a failure-path resource leak and does not alter successful-path cleanup cardinality or add expensive boundaries.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed file and all diff pages. Traced mock-editor ID consumption, outline ReferenceCollection ownership, virtual-timer failure behavior, helper callers, disposal tracking, and normal/failing lifecycle paths. No diff-introduced performance regression met the reporting threshold; no report_finding was submitted.
